text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Senior officials of the APEC forum ended on Thursday a two-day meeting after endorsing the Manila Action Plan for APEC for consideration by APEC ministers who will start their two-day meeting today. (BULLETIN/CHRONICLE)

- A pedestrian was killed and nine others were injured in separate incidents in the "Friendship Lane" on Roxas Boulevard meant for the exclusive use of APEC delegates. As a result, the Apec Organising Committee said vehicles using the special lanes would be limited to 50 kilometers per hour and violators would be arrested. (TODAY)

- The National Union of Workers in the Hotel, Restaurant and Allied Industries (Nuwhrain), the largest federation of unions in the hotel and restaurant industry, on Thursday assured the government that its members would not go on strike during the APEC meetings. (PHILIPPINE STAR,MANILA TIMES)
- President Ramos said a bomb found on Wednesday in Subic near the site of the APEC leaders' summit had been planted as part of a security exercise. (INQUIRER).
- President Ramos has expressed "complete satisfaction" with the readiness of Subic to host the 4th APEC Leaders' Meeting. (TIMES JOURNAL)

- President Ramos on Thursday defended APEC against criticism that it is just a talking shop, with non-binding agreements, saying that trade and investments in the region have improved since the formation of APEC. (MALAYA)
